Outcome_variable.extract_value: life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect
Outcome_variable.evidence_source: Life satisfaction was assessed using the Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS; Diener et al., 1985). The SWLS is a 5-item scale designed to measure global cognitive judgments of satisfaction with one’s life. Participants indicate their agreement with each item using a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree). Higher scores indicate greater life satisfaction. The SWLS has demonstrated good psychometric properties across various populations (Diener et al., 1985; Pavot & Diener, 1993). Positive and negative affect were assessed using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS; Watson et al., 1988). The PANAS consists of two 10-item mood scales, one measuring positive affect (PA) and the other negative affect (NA).
